sections.text:
The MCGG is a microprocessor based over-current relay available in single, 
 two, three or four pole versions manufactured by GEC Alsthom. Each pole is 
 provided with a choice of four inverse time characteristics and three 
 definite time characteristics as well as a trip test position.

An instantaneous element is also available on each phase. The MCGG 22 is the 
 single-phase version.

The first draft is initiated, relay tested by eng. Hany Bassuony Abdel Razek, 
 aprroved by eng. Mahmoud Badawy, and accepted by general manager eng. Gamal 
 Abdel Wahab head sector of inspection & quality control.

Preliminary 
Steps to Prepare for Relay Testing

items:
This procedure is used to perform off 
 load relay test.

The test is to determine the pick up 
 current and time.

Take a copy 
 of the relay setting.
Connect the circuit as shown in fig. 1.

Switch off the DC supply feeding the 
 relay.
Adjust the time setting to zero.

Switch on the DC supply feeding the 
 relay.
Switch on the Sverker.

Raise the current from zero slowly until 
 the relay picks up and the red led lights.
This is the pick up current.
Switch off the Sverker.

Switch off the DC supply feeding the 
 relay.

Adjust the time setting to its normal 
 value.

Switch on the DC supply feeding the 
 relay.
Short circuiting the leads of the current
Switch on the Sverker.

Adjust the current to little more than 
 the pick up current.

Switch off the 
 Sverker.
Remove the short of the current leads.

Switch on the 
 Sverker to apply the adjusted current 
 suddenly.

The relay trips after a time this is the 
 pick up time.

Compare the pick up current and pick up 
 time with the settings.
